chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Accurate T-staging is crucial for personalized treatment of laryngopharyngeal cancer. Early-stage disease is generally managed with organ-preserving surgery, laser resection, or definitive radiotherapy, whereas advanced disease often requires total laryngectomy and adjuvant treatment. Pathology-based staging is invasive and time-consuming, while manual review of an entire 3D CT volume is labor-intensive and subjective. Radiologists must track the tumor across many slices and assess extension into tightly packed adjacent structures, making borderline invasion particularly difficult to determine. Existing computer-aided approaches have two major limitations. First, whole-volume models and isolated tumor masks underrepresent the anatomy-structured pattern of tumor spread; manual tumor segmentation is also costly and difficult because tumors have heterogeneous appearances. Second, conventional multimodal methods fuse global CT and report representations, making it difficult to align individual anatomical structures with their corresponding textual findings.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the challenges of CT-based staging, the limitations of existing methods, and the need for accurate T-staging for treatment planning, aligning with the paper's description.

chk_secondary_result.poster_evidence: A whole-volume CT baseline obtains 58.76% macro F1 for binary staging and 39.16% for three-class staging. The full model with REG reaches 83.96% binary F1 and 64.53% three-class F1, with the highest mean performance and lowest variance.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: We introduce an anatomy-structured multimodal framework that integrates 3D CT volumes and radiology reports for laryngopharyngeal cancer T-staging without manual tumor masks. AOG models clinically meaningful organ topology, OCA aligns each organ with relevant report evidence, and REG injects explicit invasion findings into graph reasoning while retaining anatomy-based risk connections. Evaluation on 656 patients from four centers demonstrates consistent improvements over strong image-only and multimodal baselines in binary and three-class staging. The model generalizes to external cohorts, remains robust to segmentation noise and report variation, and performs on par with or better than experienced radiologists. Its organ-level alignment and invasion pathways also provide clinically meaningful interpretability.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster accurately summarizes the main conclusion of the paper, including the framework's performance and interpretability.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: Error analysis identifies two dominant patterns. Nine of sixteen errors are over-staging cases, often caused by reports describing cartilage invasion that pathology does not confirm. Seven are under-staging cases, frequently associated with reports that omit invasion or state that invasion is absent despite pathological confirmation. These findings reflect inherent CT-pathology discordance rather than simple cross-modal misalignment and motivate uncertainty-aware fusion and clinical review of borderline cases.
chk_limitation.reason: The poster mentions the limitations of CT-based assessment, including over-staging and under-staging, which align with the paper's description.
